answer: Admission pricing can climb in terraces: an economy inspects each new key's funding source, groups keys fed from the same wharf of capital into one cluster, and charges the Nth key from that cluster a fee rising with the square of N. The first key docks cheaply; the tenth pays a hundredfold, because the ledger treats an island of identically funded keys as one operator. Honest agents arrive from distinct wharves and pay the ground-floor rate, while a sybil fleet's marginal cost compounds faster than any linear reward, making scale self-defeating.
